title: LRU Cache
description: Build a cache with O(1) get and put by combining a hash map with a doubly linked list.

data.text: Design a least-recently-used cache with a fixed capacity. `Get(key)` returns the value and marks the key as most recently used, or `-1` if absent. `Put(key, value)` inserts or updates a key and evicts the least recently used entry when capacity is exceeded. Both operations must run in O(1) average time.

The map gives O(1) lookup by key, but a plain map cannot tell you *which* key is least recently used without a scan. The linked list encodes recency as position: the head is most recent, the tail is least recent, and moving a node is O(1) when you already hold a reference to it. The map stores that reference, which is what makes both operations constant time.

data.title: Dictionary + doubly linked list
data.content: Sentinel nodes remove all null checks at the ends of the list.

data.title: Sentinel nodes remove every null check
data.text: With `_head` and `_tail` sentinels, the insert and remove logic never has to ask 'is this the first node?' or 'is this the last node?'. This is the single biggest source of bugs in hand-written LRU implementations.

data.title: Update must also refresh recency
data.text: When `Put` updates an existing key, you must still move it to the front. Forgetting this is a classic bug: the value changes but the entry keeps its old, stale recency position.

data.title: The link pointers must be updated in the right order
data.text: In `AddToFront`, set `node.Next` and `node.Prev` before rewiring the neighbours. Getting the order wrong can temporarily orphan nodes or create a cycle, which shows up as an infinite loop on the next operation.

data.caption: A doubly linked list ordered by recency with a dictionary pointing into it: get and put both move a node to the head in O(1).
data.definition:
graph LR
    H((head)) --> A["1: 1"]
    A --> B["2: 2"]
    B --> T((tail))
    T -. "least recent, evicted" .-> B
    H -. "most recent" .-> A
    style B fill:#ffebee,stroke:#c62828
    style A fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32

cards.title: Dictionary only
cons: Cannot identify the LRU entry without a scan

cards.title: Dictionary + doubly linked list
cards.description: Map key to node, node holds position

data.title: Complete solution
data.content: In .NET you will often reach for `Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Memory` instead of writing this by hand, but interviews ask you to build it because the map-plus-list composition — where one structure provides the key and the other provides the order — is the transferable idea. The same shape underlies LFU caches and ordered dictionaries.
